You are building verification tooling for a large refactoring project on treams-rs (treams-rs; Rust core crates/treams-core, PyO3 bindings crates/treams-py -> python/treams_rs/_native, Python package python/treams_rs). Read decisions.md and sections §8 (Gates and tools) and §10.1/§10.2 of plan.md first. You implement the lead's stage-0 tooling tasks 2 and 5 of §10.1 (NOT the CHANGELOG, venv installs or target pruning — the lead does those concurrently; do not touch treams-rs's working tree, battery.py, parity/*.npz, or anything under benchmarks/results).

Context you need:

  • scratch: wt.sh is the helper every implementation lane uses (lanes are git worktrees under scratch: lanes/<name>, created later from the integration branch claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh). Read it fully. It refuses to run in the main checkout treams-rs. It already has: build-ext, build-ext-release, pytest, python, rust-test, rust-fmt, rust-lint, rust-doc, py-fmt, py-lint, py-types, docs, docs-check, gates, full, parity, bitwise, clean.
  • Reference tree: treams (Python original): r4 = detached worktree at 5fe22f4 (condensed into 8251007) with a RELEASE extension in treams (Python original): r4/python/treams_rs/. The bitwise battery recording at 5fe22f4 (condensed into 8251007) is r4.npz (RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1; battery.py compare r4.npz --rtol 0 --atol-scale 0 gives 0 failing on both release and dev builds).
  • Existing dump tools: U1/dump.py (ufuncs, fast paths, every battery case with pullback probes, record validation; python dump.py OUT.pkl, python dump.py --compare A.pkl B.pkl; it loads the battery from the hard-coded path battery.py at line ~78) plus run_dump.sh/compare.sh/module_meta.py next to it; C1/dump.py (lattice sums; dump.py record OUT, dump.py compare A B). Timing tools: P1/ab.py (interleaved A/B, see its docstring; --a/--b take directories with python/ and scripts/), cg.sh (callgrind per-call instruction counts; CG_CPU env), cg_driver.py, cpu_harness.py.
  • Machine: 4 CPUs, ~14 GB free disk. Shared venv .venv (never pip/uv install into it; the lead does installs).

Deliver:

  1. Upgrade scratch: wt.sh per plan §8.3 (keep every existing command working and its behaviour; keep the main-checkout guard):
    • CPU pinning: cargo and pytest under taskset -c 0-2 with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 (CPU 3 is reserved for timing).
    • build-ext: if so/current/ exists and records a merge sha M (file sha), and git diff --quiet M -- crates Cargo.toml Cargo.lock holds in the lane (and M is an ancestor of HEAD), copy the cached debug .so instead of compiling; otherwise compile as today. Add publish-so (lead use: copy this tree's built debug .so to so/<HEAD sha>/ with a sha file and repoint the current symlink) — the lead will also call it from the main checkout, so allow it (and only it, plus read-only commands you think are safe) to run there via an explicit flag or env var such as WT_ALLOW_MAIN=1.
    • docs / docs-check: run scripts/generate_docs.py if it exists, else scripts/generate_agent_docs.py (same flags).
    • docs-build: mkdocs build --strict with scratch: docs-venv/bin/mkdocs (the lead builds that venv; if mkdocs.yml is absent print a note and succeed). docs-rust: treams-core rustdoc with private items into site/rust. docs-examples: scripts/generate_docs.py --examples (fail clearly if the script is absent).
    • rust-doc-private: RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items --locked.
    • rust-test-list: cargo test --locked -p treams-core -- --list normalised (sorted test names, one per line, no counts footer) to stdout.
    • ids: sorted pytest node ids (pytest --collect-only -q lines that contain '::') plus a final line skipped-at-collection: N and then, separately, the number of tests skipped in a full run is NOT needed here; also provide ids --skips that runs the full suite with -rs -q and prints the skip count (slow; documented).
    • lock [--check]: uv lock / uv lock --check using uv from PATH (the lead confirms uv 0.12.3 is available; print its version first). It must only touch uv.lock.
    • bitwise: keep as is, but default the battery to the CURRENT gate kit's battery (gates/current/battery.py) when present, else battery.py; --battery PATH overrides.
    • uf, lat, hot: record the U1, C1 and hot-path dumps from the lane tree with the current kit's scripts at RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1, and compare them with the kit's r4 recordings through the kit's key/message map (map.json: old->new key renames and old->new message text replacements applied to the r4 side before comparing). Every numeric byte must be identical; print a summary and list differences; exit nonzero on any difference not covered by the map.
    • kit-copy: copy the current kit into scratch<lane name>-kit/ for lane-local adaptation, and document how a package writes its patch to gates/patches/<ID>.diff (a diff -ruN of the kit dir vs the lane-local copy) — add a kit-diff <ID> command that writes that patch.
    • perf-ab <workload> [args], perf-cg <fwd|bwd> <workload> [args], perf-illum: perf-station commands per plan §8.4: take flock perf.lock; in the perf worktree lanes/perf, git checkout --detach <calling lane HEAD sha> (the lanes share the object store), build the release extension there (cargo build --locked --release -p treams-py --features extension-module and copy target/release/lib_native.so into python/treams_rs/), then run ab.py with --cputime --cpu 3 --pairs 6 --a treams (Python original): r4 --b lanes/perf -- <workload> [args] (write records to a per-lane jsonl under perf/), or cg.sh with CG_CPU=3 for both treams (Python original): r4 and lanes/perf, printing both counts and the relative difference. perf-illum runs scripts/benchmark_illumination.py's default case in both trees interleaved (read that script to find how; 6 pairs, CPU 3, CPU time if feasible) and prints median ratios. Make sure the perf worktree's checkout cannot disturb lanes (it is its own worktree) and that a failed build releases the lock.
  2. Create the perf station: git -C treams-rs worktree add --detach lanes/perf 5fe22f4 (condensed into 8251007) (if it does not exist), and create perf.lock (empty file). Verify perf-cg on one small workload end to end (e.g. wt.sh perf-cg fwd sw-translate or whatever workload names cg_driver.py/benchmark_cluster.py accept — find a cheap one) from a temporary detached worktree of 5fe22f4 (condensed into 8251007) that you create under lanes/tooltest and REMOVE afterwards (git worktree remove --force). The release build takes ~5 min; keep target (the perf station's only release target) but delete target/release/{deps,build,incremental} leftovers you do not need only if disk gets tight (check df).
  3. Gate kit v0 at gates/5fe22f4 (condensed into 8251007)/ with current -> that directory:
    • battery.py: a copy of battery.py (unchanged).
    • uf_dump.py: a copy of U1/dump.py whose battery path is a command-line parameter (default: the battery.py next to it), same encoding; compare mode as before.
    • lat_dump.py: a copy of C1/dump.py.
    • hot_dump.py: NEW targeted hot-path dump (plan §8.1 GATE-HOT), recording raw bytes of values AND pullbacks (with fixed random cotangents) through the public/diff API at 5fe22f4 (condensed into 8251007) names: S-matrix add and illuminate above 512 rows with at most 8 columns (the Krylov branch of crates/treams-core/src/smatrix/internal.rs — read it to choose sizes that really take that branch, and also one case just below the switch); the matrix-free iterative sphere cluster (python/treams_rs/iterative.py SphereCluster) solve and solve-with-pullback through GMRES with 16 or more spheres; InteractionFactor.record (diff.factor_interaction) with its pullback; ebcm qmat with legacy=False and legacy=True (the flag will later be renamed radial_area_factor; record under neutral keys) with pullbacks; field sampling at 2048 points (spherical and cylindrical waves, through the public field API or diff.field). Read the code to find the right entry points and keep each case fast (< ~10 s at 1 thread with a dev build). Keys must be stable names; structure like uf_dump.py's enc().
    • map.json: {"keys": {}, "messages": {}} (empty for v0) and a README.md explaining the kit, the map semantics and the patch protocol.
    • r4 recordings: run uf_dump.py, lat_dump.py and hot_dump.py against treams (Python original): r4 (PYTHONPATH=treams (Python original): r4/python, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1) into r4.uf.pkl, r4.lat.pkl, r4.hot.pkl in the kit dir, run each a second time and confirm the re-run compares identical (report any nondeterministic keys and exclude them deliberately, documented in README.md). Then confirm that a DEV build of the same commit compares identical too: build one in your temporary tooltest worktree (wt.sh build-ext there) and run wt.sh uf, wt.sh lat, wt.sh hot, wt.sh bitwise from it — all must report 0 differences.
  4. Report: the final wt.sh command list with one line each, the kit contents, the r4 recording sizes/entry counts, the verification results (exact command outputs summarised), anything nondeterministic you excluded, timings of each command, and any caveat. Leave no temporary worktrees behind (except lanes/perf), and keep so/ empty except what publish-so creates (do not publish anything yourself unless testing publish-so in the tooltest worktree, in which case remove the test entry afterwards).

Stage-0 tooling report: §10.1 tasks 2 and 5 (wt.sh upgrade, perf station, gate kit v0)

All of it is in place and verified end to end. A dev build of 5fe22f4 (condensed into 8251007) reports 0 differences on bitwise, uf, lat and hot. perf-cg gives identical counts for the same commit. Before you rely on the gates, read caveat 1: pinning lanes to 3 CPUs breaks the bitwise battery unless BLAS is held to one thread. wt.sh now does that.

1. scratch: wt.sh (394 lines)

  • I installed it with an atomic mv, so shells already running the old script are not disturbed.
  • The pre-upgrade copy is at tools/wt.sh.orig.
  • Cargo, pytest and python run under taskset -c 0-2 with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3.
  • The main-checkout guard is kept. With WT_ALLOW_MAIN=1 only these run in the main checkout: help, publish-so, ids, rust-test-list, docs-check, lock --check, parity, bitwise, uf, lat, hot, perf-ab, perf-cg, perf-illum.

Commands:

  • build-ext: compiles the debug extension, or copies so/current/lib_native.so when so/current/sha is an ancestor of HEAD, git diff --quiet M -- crates Cargo.toml Cargo.lock holds and there are no untracked files there. WT_NO_SO_CACHE=1 forces a compile. The .so is installed with tmp+mv, so running Pythons keep the old file.
  • build-ext-release: unchanged, perf station only.
  • publish-so (lead): refuses if crates/Cargo.* have uncommitted changes. Otherwise runs cargo build (a no-op when fresh), copies target/debug/lib_native.so to so/<HEAD sha>/ with sha and info files, and swaps the current symlink atomically.
  • pytest, python, rust-test, rust-fmt, rust-lint, rust-doc, py-fmt, py-lint, py-types, parity, clean: as before, pinned.
  • rust-doc-private: RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --document-private-items --locked.
  • rust-test-list: sorted test names, doctest " (line N)" suffix stripped, no footer.
  • docs / docs-check: use scripts/generate_docs.py if it exists, else generate_agent_docs.py; arguments pass through.
  • docs-build: scratch: docs-venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict, with the Material "MkDocs 2.0" banner silenced. Succeeds with a note when mkdocs.yml is absent.
  • docs-rust: treams-core rustdoc with private items into site/rust, plus an index redirect. Run it after docs-build, because docs-build cleans site/.
  • docs-examples: runs generate_docs.py --examples, or fails clearly while the script is absent.
  • ids: sorted node ids plus skipped-at-collection: N, where N is the sum of the SKIPPED [n] lines (with -q, pytest's footer omits skips). ids --skips runs the full suite with -q -rs and prints the SKIPPED lines and skipped: N (slow).
  • lock [--check]: prints the uv version, then runs uv lock [--check] --python <venv python>. It takes uv from the original PATH, sets UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never, and fails if anything other than uv.lock changed.
  • gates: now also runs rust-doc, rust-doc-private and docs-build, per GATE-FULL in §8.1. full = gates + pytest -x + parity.
  • bitwise: uses the battery of the resolved kit; --battery PATH or --kit DIR override.
  • uf, lat, hot:
    • record the dump at RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 into scratch<lane>-gates/ (the panic noise on stderr goes to <kind>.stderr);
    • then run the kit's kitcmp.py against r4.<kind>.pkl through map.json;
    • exit nonzero on any difference not covered by the map.
  • Kit resolution: --kit DIR > $WT_KIT > scratch<lane>-kit > gates/current. A stale local kit (copied from an older kit) is refused.
  • kit-copy [--force]: copies the scripts, symlinks the r4 recordings and records the source kit in .kit-source.
  • kit-diff <ID>: writes diff -ruN a/ b/ to gates/patches/<ID>.diff, which applies with patch -p1.
  • perf-ab [--pairs N] <workload> [args], perf-cg <fwd|bwd> <workload> [args], perf-illum [case args]:
    • flock -o perf.lock; prints who holds it while waiting; holder written to perf/holder;
    • git -C lanes/perf checkout --detach --force <HEAD> (warns that uncommitted changes are not measured);
    • pinned release build, .so copied, release profile asserted;
    • then ab.py (--cputime --cpu 3 --pairs 6), cg.sh with CG_CPU=3 on both trees, or tools/illum_ab.py;
    • records go to perf/<lane>{.jsonl,.cg.jsonl,.illum.jsonl}.
    • A failure at any step exits and releases the lock; verified with a bad workload and with a forced cargo failure.
  • Unknown commands now print help and exit 2 (they used to exit 0, which made typos look like success).

illum_ab.py runs the script's own --worker mode:

  • backends full, selected and matrix-free × phases forward and adjoint;
  • 6 interleaved pairs on CPU 3, process CPU time, --threads 1, the script's default case;
  • prints the medians, ratio of medians, pair-median and per-pair ratios for fresh/reuse/setup/backward, and checks the output arrays are bitwise identical A/B.

2. Perf station

  • lanes/perf is a detached worktree at 5fe22f4 (condensed into 8251007) with a release target (435 MB; no pruning was needed, 17 GB free).
  • perf.lock exists and is empty.

3. Gate kit v0: gates/5fe22f4/ (condensed into 8251007) (current points to it), 39 MB

File What it is
battery.py identical to battery.py
uf_dump.py U1 dump with --battery (defaults to the battery next to it) and the same enc (change below)
lat_dump.py C1 dump, plus a __codes__ entry (change below)
hot_dump.py new, 21 cases (below)
kitcmp.py comparator that applies the map
map.json {"keys": {}, "messages": {}}
README.md kit, determinism notes, map semantics, patch and merge protocol
gates/patches/ empty, ready for package patches
  • uf_dump.py change: each ufunc now seeds its own input generator from its name, and NATIVE_ALIASES maps a renamed ufunc to its r4 name. Renaming or removing one ufunc no longer shifts every other ufunc's inputs.
  • lat_dump.py change: __codes__ lists the text behind each crc32 error code folded into the arrays, so message changes inside arrays can be mapped.
  • hot_dump.py cases:
    • S-matrix add at n=512.
    • Illuminate:
      • Krylov branch: n512p8, n640p1, zero right-hand sides;
      • LU branch: 511 rows, 9 columns, not a contraction;
      • Krylov fallback to LU: contraction that does not converge in 16 steps.
    • Public SMatrix.add / illuminate(smat=...).
    • 16-sphere iterative.SphereCluster: solve, restarted solve, solve_with_pullback (lmax 2 and 3), scatter; 14–16 GMRES iterations each.
    • factor_interaction dense, block and cluster_factor, and diff.illuminate, with record and pullbacks.
    • ebcm_qmat / ebcm.qmat with and without the area factor, regular and singular. Keys say with_area_factor / without_area_factor.
    • Fields at 2048 points, spherical and cylindrical: diff.field and field_operator with pullback and pullback_axial, plus public efield/hfield.
    • I confirmed the Krylov/LU dispatch with gdb breakpoints on internal_iteration and Lu::new in the debug build.
    • Arrays over 2 MiB (22 of them) are stored as a SHA-256 of the raw bytes plus a 4096-element sample; everything else is raw bytes.
  • map.json optional sections: kitcmp also accepts key_patterns, message_patterns, new_keys and exclude. v0 contains only the two required sections.

4. Verification (dev build in lanes/tooltest, since removed)

  • Dev gates vs r4:
    • wt.sh hot: 225 identical, OK (11.5 s).
    • wt.sh uf: 25515 identical, OK (24 s).
    • wt.sh lat: 11929 identical, OK (7 min 1 s).
    • wt.sh bitwise: 128 cases, 0 failing, PASS (11 s).
  • Collection and listing:
    • ids: 4558 ids, skipped-at-collection: 0 (7.5 s).
    • ids --skips: 4536 passed, 22 skipped, all at test_ufunc_contract.py:773 (3 min 52 s). The full suite passes under pinning.
    • rust-test-list: 216 names, no doctests (0.6 s once compiled).
  • Docs and lock:
    • lock --check and lock: OK, uv.lock unchanged.
    • docs-check: "Agent documentation is current".
    • docs-build: no-op, then a strict build with a temporary mkdocs.yml (1 s).
    • docs-rust: 2 min 5 s.
    • rust-doc-private: passes at 5fe22f4 (condensed into 8251007) (52 s).
    • docs-examples: fails clearly, as intended.
  • Kit handling: kit-copy, auto-detection of the local kit, refusal of a stale kit, and kit-diff; the patch passes patch -p1 --dry-run.
  • Map logic: a synthetic lane with renames, a removal, message changes and a new key gave OK with the map and fails without it. A changed numeric byte is caught.
  • publish-so and the .so cache: publish-so created the cache entry; build-ext then reused it (0.26 s, byte-identical), and refused it after a crates/ edit. The test entry is removed, so so/ is empty.
  • perf-cg fwd bessel-forward --samples 64:
    • first run 7 min 46 s, of which the release build took 6 min 37 s;
    • later runs about 70 s;
    • r4 460055 vs lane 460055, +0.000%.
  • perf-cg bwd bessel: −0.071% and +0.002% on two runs of the same commit.
  • perf-ab --pairs 2: plumbing works (3.8 s).
  • perf-illum: 2 min 7 s; outputs bitwise identical A/B for all 6 combinations. Same-commit pair-medians ranged 0.97–1.04 while pytest ran on CPUs 0–2; the roughly 1 ms "reuse" metrics are pure noise.
  • Lock behaviour: a second perf command waited, failed, and released the lock.

Caveats

  1. BLAS threads (important). OpenBLAS sizes its pool from CPU affinity. Under taskset -c 0-2 it uses 3 threads, and battery case cluster_physics_workflow then fails bitwise (global_expand and interaction.call differ by about 1e-21). With 1 or 4 threads it passes. wt.sh therefore sets OPENBLAS/OMP/MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 for parity, bitwise, uf, lat and hot; under that the full battery passes and parity shows only the 2 accepted failures. Anyone running the battery by hand under pinning must do the same.
  2. Callgrind is sensitive to environment and path length. Per-call counts moved by about ±1.5% with environment size or root-path length, and I once saw 163k vs 463k in different invocations. perf runs therefore use equal-length symlinks (cg/{r4,la}), and perf-cg runs cg.sh under env -i from a fixed directory. With that, fwd counts are identical for the same commit; bwd still varies by about 0.1% run to run.
  3. perf-ab noise at the same commit reaches about 4% when lanes are busy on CPUs 0–2. This matters against the 3% and 2% thresholds.
  4. U1 key collisions. U1 already records both angular_value.* and angular_scalar.*, so the R50c renames must adapt call sites and keep keys. kitcmp refuses a map that sends two r4 keys to one new key.
  5. Disk. The debug .so is 305 MB, so each so/<sha> costs that much and each cache copy into a lane does too. uv prints a deprecation warning about UV_NATIVE_TLS from the environment; it is harmless.
  6. What is left behind. No temporary worktrees remain except lanes/perf; so/ and perf/ are empty. cg holds the symlinks that wt.sh recreates on each perf run.
